text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Foreign Minister Bouez heads to Damascus today to discuss with Syrian officials the tense situation in south Lebanon.
-President Hrawi said that the arrest campaign following attacks on Syrian targets in Lebanon last month could have been done with a fewer number of mistakes.
-Banque de la Mediterranee, Lebanon's biggest bank, has more than doubled its capital to $212 million, Chairman Razian said.

-A general assembly of the shareholders of Lebanon's cargo carrier Trans Mediterranean Airlines (TMA) will be held on January 31 to discuss the company's plan to increase its capital, TMA's board said.
-The Lebanese-Syrian coordination committee which includes ministers from both sides will meet in Damascus on Saturday to discuss several bilateral agreements.
-Today's cabinet meeting is postponed due to the crisis between the army and the government regarding the promotion of some high ranking officers.

-The five-nation ceasefire monitoring committee in south Lebanon has started its meetings to study three Israeli and three Lebanese complaints over alleged breaches of the U.S.-brokered ceasefire understanding that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz last April.
